subject: Demo recap + proposed mini-pilot (evaluation sprint) — Citrine Health
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Carter <alyssa@citrinehealth.com>, Devon Li <devon@citrinehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-12T14:14:00-07:00
Subject: Demo recap + proposed mini-pilot (evaluation sprint) — Citrine Health

Thanks again for the demo today — great conversation. I captured a short recap and a proposed mini-pilot (4-week evaluation sprint) below so we can align on success criteria, owners, and next steps. I attached a one-page outline and a simple evaluation matrix for you to share internally (attached: citrine-mini-pilot-outline.docx, evaluation-matrix.xlsx).

Recap (what we heard)
- Goal: Reduce clinical triage time for inbound referral messages by surfacing relevant patient context and suggested dispositions to triage nurses.
- Data: Real-time EHR summaries + referral metadata (no PHI to Redwood; we’ll run in your VPC or dedicated environment).
- KPIs: Triage latency, suggestion acceptance rate, and error rate on suggested dispositions.

Proposed mini-pilot (4 weeks) — high level
1) Week 0 (kickoff, tech onboarding) — 2-hour technical kickoff, vault/KMS setup, sample payload schema, test endpoint access. Owner: Karthik (solutions).
2) Week 1 (integration + smoke) — send synthetic test stream, validate message schemas, run 48-hour smoke on 500 messages. Owner: Devon (Citrine), Karthik (Redwood).
3) Week 2 (closed eval) — run evaluation against labeled set (1k items) to measure baseline vs model suggestions. Owner: Alyssa / Devon.
4) Week 3 (live shadow) — shadow mode on a subset (5% traffic), collect acceptance metrics and clinician feedback. Owner: Alyssa.
5) Week 4 (wrap & decision) — present evaluation results, recommended config for production, and optional contract terms. Owner: Sergio / Priyom.

Success criteria (pass/fail thresholds)
- Triage latency: 20% reduction vs baseline on average.
- Suggestion acceptance: >= 55% during shadow window.
- Safety filter: < 1% flagged for manual review.

Risks & mitigations
- Data schema drift — include schema validation + quick rollback.
- Clinician trust — manual feedback loop and short feedback cadence to iterate prompts.

Required things from Citrine to start
- Test API credentials (or VPC peering details) and a sample of anonymized/hashed payloads (Devon).
- Point of contact for clinical review during week 3 (Alyssa).
- PO or procurement signal for trial duration (Tom).

Next steps (suggested)
- If this looks good, can we schedule the 2-hour technical kickoff for next week? I’m available Tue/Wed afternoon PST.
- I’ll upload the one-page outline and the evaluation matrix to the Drive link below for your procurement team.

Thanks — happy to tighten the scope if you’d prefer a shorter 2-week sprint.

—
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0198

Attachments: citrine-mini-pilot-outline.docx (docx, 1 page), evaluation-matrix.xlsx (xlsx, 5 rows)

Thanks, Sergio — this is very helpful and aligns with what the clinical team wants to see. Quick clarifications: 
1) For "no PHI to Redwood" — procurement will want the exact data flow diagram and assurance that keys remain in our KMS. Can you confirm you can run in our VPC with customer-managed keys?
2) For success criteria, can we add a qualitative clinician trust survey (5-question form) during week 3? We want subjective acceptance in addition to the numeric acceptance rate.

We are generally good to move forward. Tom (procurement) — can you confirm whether a short trial MSA or SOW is sufficient, or if procurement needs a PO up front?

Also schedule-wise, Wed 09/15 10:00–12:00 PST works for our engineers for the 2-hr kickoff.

—
Alyssa Carter
Director, Clinical Products
Citrine Health
alyssa@citrinehealth.com

Thanks Alyssa & Tom — great questions. Quick answers below, and I attached a short SOW draft and the data-flow diagram (attached: redwood-trial-sla.pdf).

1) VPC + KMS: Yes — we support a private deployment model where the runtime runs in your VPC and keys remain customer-managed. We will not persist PHI outside your environment; we can add explicit language in the SOW + indemnity clause.
2) Clinician trust survey: Absolutely — we'll add a 5-question short form and include that in the Week 3 collection.
3) Ballpark cost at 5% live traffic: approximately $4k–$7k/month depending on batching and quantization profile; Priyom can run a quick config estimate once we agree traffic assumptions.
